_comment: Baseline for core/brain/tests/recall_perf_100k.rs. `cold` / `warm` are the fallback path (query with no time/app filter → full KNN over 100K vectors); `cold_scoped` / `warm_scoped` are the ADR-0011 §5 candidate-pool pre-filter path (query with realistic app + time scope, i.e. 'in Safari' + 'last 24 hours'). The scoped numbers are the ones the production user experiences on the common case (recent / focused searches). Regenerate with `MCI_PERF_UPDATE_BASELINE=1 cargo test --profile=perf -p mci-brain -- --ignored recall_perf_100k::run` on the reference machine.
_captured_on: Apple M-series MacBook Pro, on-battery, cold shell
_notes: ADR-0011 §5 candidate-pool pre-filter (cycle 8.56) closes the 100K-events perf gap on scoped queries: cold_scoped P50 106ms and warm_scoped P99 127ms are all inside the advisory budgets (cold 200ms / warm-P50 50ms / warm-P99 500ms).

Unscoped queries (`cold` / `warm`) still exercise the full-KNN fallback because the pre-filter cannot narrow when the caller supplies no time / app scope. Cold P50 387ms remains > 200ms budget — the next lever for the unscoped path is binary quantization (~10x brute-force speedup) per ADR-0011 §5.

warm P50 (unscoped) 342ms is dominated by the 100K-row cosine loop, not by SQLite or FTS5. Binary quantization is the next scaling-ladder step; it is out of scope for this PR (which is scoped to ~250 LOC of the pre-filter lever).
The harness intentionally does NOT fail on budget breach — this file is the regression baseline; per-path budgets are enforced by the eventual CI diff-vs-baseline job.
